'''Evelyn Berezin''' (April 12, 1925 - December 8, 2018) was an American [[Computer engineer|computer designer]] responsible for the creation of the first [[Airline reservation system|airline reservation systems]]<ref name="Reservisor2">{{Cite journal |last=Eklund |first=Jon |date=1994 |title=The Reservisor automated airline reservation system: combining communications and computing |journal=IEEE Annals of the History of Computing |volume=16 |pages=62–69 |doi=10.1109/85.251855 |s2cid=16465013 |quote=Shortly after the beginnings of the computer in the mid-1940s, a machine appeared that was the first in a long line of important commercial systems integrating communications and processing: the Reservisor airline reservation system built by the Teleregister Corporation.}}</ref> and the original [[word processor]].<ref name="witi2">{{cite web |title=Evelyn Berezin |url=https://www.witi.com/halloffame/303047/Evelyn-Berezin-Management-Consultant-Brookhaven-Science-Associates/ |work=WITI Hall of Fame |publisher=Women in Technology International}}</ref><ref name="McFadden2">{{cite news |author=McFadden, Robert D. |date=2018-12-10 |title=Evelyn Berezin, 93, Dies; Built the First True Word Processor |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/12/10/obituaries/evelyn-berezin-dead.html |accessdate=2018-12-18 |work=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Born and raised in [[East Bronx]] on 1925,<ref>{{cite web |title=WOMAN IN BUSINESS |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1972/02/20/archives/doing-it-herself-miss-berezin-decided-to-form-a-concern.html |website=New York Times |access-date=30 September 2026}}</ref> Berezin attended [[Christopher Columbus High School (Bronx)|Christopher Columbus High School]].<ref name="McFadden2" /> Born to a working-class family with [[History of the Jews in Belarus|Belarusian Jewish]] immigrant parents, her father Soloman was a furrier and her mother Rose a seamstress. Early on she became enamored with science and technology after reading her older brother’s copies of ''[[Analog Science Fiction and Fact|Astounding Science Fiction]]'' magazines.<ref name="McFadden2" /> During her high school years this love for technology grew. When she was 16, Berezin enrolled at [[Hunter College]] where she was offered a position as a lab technician but also took courses at [[New York University]] (NYU).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Evelyn Berezin {{!}} The National Inventors Hall of Fame |url=https://www.invent.org/inductees/evelyn-berezin |access-date=2022-04-21 |website=www.invent.org |language=en}}</ref> In 1945, she earned a [[bachelor’s degree]] in physics<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-04-04 |title=Evelyn Berezin |url=https://computerhistory.org/profile/evelyn-berezin/?alias=bio&person=evelyn-berezin |access-date=2025-04-13 |website=CHM |language=en}}</ref> and a doctorate in the same field. In 1951, she began working in the computer industry. Working at different companies is where she learned about [[logic design]] and system development. She was often the only woman in technical teams. 

Simultaneously, she was working full-time in the [[Rheology]] Department as an assistant for an International Printing Company known at the time as IPI. Evelyn earned her [[Bachelor of Science|B.S]]. in physics in the year 1946<ref name="McFadden2" /> and would go on to make significant contributions within the space.<ref name="McFadden2" />

==Innovations==
Berezin already held a fellowship from the [[United States Atomic Energy Commission]] during her days at NYU.<ref name="SION2">{{cite web |title=About Sion Power |url=https://sionpower.com/about/ |access-date=December 18, 2018 |website=Sion Power |df=dmy-all}}</ref> A startup from Brooklyn by the name of Electronic Computer Corporation<ref name="c501">{{cite web |title=New Computer Concern Set Up |website=The New York Times |date=1950-01-24 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1950/01/24/archives/new-computer-concern-set-up.html |access-date=2026-02-12}}</ref> offered Berezin an opportunity to become the head of the Logistic Design Department in 1951 which she accepted even though she lacked experience in computer design. This was due to her struggle to find work within the physics world. It was a blessing in disguise as she went on to design many types of computers for different purposes including what we currently know as the office computer.<ref name="witi2" /> In 1957, Berezin left her job at the [[Underwood Typewriter Company]] Company, the company that had purchased ECC at the time. She then began her work as head of logic design at a previous division of [[Western Union]]<ref name="Teleregister2">{{Cite web |date=December 7, 2018 |title=Teleregister Corporation |url=http://www.computerhistory.org/brochures/t-z/teleregister-corporation/ |accessdate=December 16, 2018 |publisher=Computer History Museum |quote=In 1948, Western Union established one of their divisions, Teleregister, as a separate company.Berezin began to work at Teleregister Corporation where she was the head of logic design. Its communications expertise gave it a prominent position in the uniting of elementary data processing and data transmission. It produced display units for stock brokers, and, in 1952, created a seat management system for the American Airlines New York Office.}}</ref> known as Teleregister where she went on to aid in the creation of the [[Reservisor]], the original [[Airline reservation system|airline reservation systems]].<ref name="Reservisor2" /> Berezin was tasked with developing one of the biggest computer systems in that era. She helped make the reservation system for [[United Airlines]] by utilizing the novel [[transistor]] technology at the time to create the [[Reservisor]] which had a one second response time.<ref name="CHM20152">{{Cite web |last=CHM |title=Evelyn Berezin — 2015 Fellow |url=http://www.computerhistory.org/fellowawards/hall/bios/Evelyn,Berezin/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150202091047/http://www.computerhistory.org/fellowawards/hall/bios/Evelyn,Berezin/ |archive-date=2015-02-02 |accessdate=March 27, 2015 |website=Computer History Museum |quote=Transistors became available in about 1957-58 and the breadth of capability suddenly expanded substantially. Computers were much faster and communication systems started to become particularly important. Berezin, then at Teleregister in Connecticut, designed one of the largest systems built at that time: a passenger reservations system for United Airlines, delivered in about 1962.}}[http://www.computerhistory.org/fellowawards/hall/bios/Evelyn,Berezin/] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150403134557/http://www.computerhistory.org/fellowawards/hall/bios/Evelyn,Berezin/|date=2015-04-03}}</ref> During her time at Teleregister, she also helped with making the first computerized banking system that many businesses went on to utilize.<ref name="Domske2">{{cite news |author=Camila Domonske |date=2018-12-12 |title=Evelyn Berezin, Computer Scientist Behind Groundbreaking Word Processor, Dies At 93 |url=https://www.npr.org/2018/12/12/676024428/evelyn-berezin-computer-scientist-behind-groundbreaking-word-processor-dies-at-9 |access-date=2018-12-13 |work=[[National Public Radio]]}}</ref>

The [[New York Stock Exchange]] even reached out with a job offer in 1960. Unfortunately, due to the fact that she was a woman, it was quickly retracted.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |last=Domonoske |first=Camila |date=2018-12-12 |title=Evelyn Berezin, Computer Scientist Behind Groundbreaking Word Processor, Dies At 93 |url=https://www.npr.org/2018/12/12/676024428/evelyn-berezin-computer-scientist-behind-groundbreaking-word-processor-dies-at-9 |access-date=2022-04-21 |work=NPR |language=en}}</ref>

In 1968, Berezin attempted to address the pain points of working as a secretary such as needing to completely retype documents when an error was found or wanting to make changes. She created the first computerized word processor and dubbed it the Data Secretary.<ref name=":1" /> In 1969, to sell her innovation, Berezin founded a company known as Redactron Corporation.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Pozzi |first=Sandro |date=December 12, 2018 |title=Muere Evelyn Berezin, creadora del primer procesador digital de textos |trans-title=Evelyn Berezin dies, creator of the first digital text processor |url=https://elpais.com/tecnologia/2018/12/11/actualidad/1544546267_076535.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181212182024/https://elpais.com/tecnologia/2018/12/11/actualidad/1544546267_076535.html |archive-date=December 12, 2018 |access-date=December 13, 2018 |website=[[El País]] |language=es |quote=Berezin diseñó el primer sistema central de reservas de United Airlines cuando trabajaba para Teleregister y otro similar para gestionar la contabilidad de la banca a nivel nacional. En 1968 empezó a trabajar en la idea de un ordenador que procesara textos, utilizando pequeños circuitos integrados. Al año decidió dejar la empresa para crear la suya propia, que llamó Redactron Corporation. |df=dmy-all}}</ref><ref name="SION2" /> Her device was similar size to that of a small refrigerator at the time, and used an [[IBM Selectric typewriter]] for its input text that would then be stored in document form on a [[tape drive]].<ref name="McFadden2" />

==Impact==
The applications of Berezin's innovations were plentiful. Her Data Secretary replaced the old process for completing important work tasks like drafting letters and reports and made it much more simple and efficient, contributing to greater productivity and saving a significant amount of time.<ref name=":0" /> It was a precursor to the hardware and software used in today's computer systems. The [[Reservisor]] meant that reservations no longer required the same manual input. This significantly improved the customer experience and was able to reduce errors, making the process more streamlined. Its impressive response time and computing features made it revolutionary to the industry.<ref name="CHM20152" /> Coupled with the breaking of gender barriers of the time her creations have had a significant impact on society today. They are both still in use, rather in a transformed state with the improved modern day technology involved. For example, Airline reservation systems are linked at a global scale. The interconnectedness of the modern world would not have been possible if it were not for her initial [[airline reservation system]]. Both innovations have seamlessly integrated within societies everyday functions and the business and travel worlds could have both been significantly different without her.

== Personal life ==
In 1951, Berezin married Israel Wilenitz. Their marriage lasted 51 years until Wilenitz died on February 20 of 2003.<ref name="wilenitz2">{{cite news |date=23 February 2003 |title=Paid Notice:Deaths Wilentitz, Israel |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2003/02/23/classified/paid-notice-deaths-wilenitz-israel.html |work=The New York Times}}</ref> Berezin died 15 years later whilst being treated for cancer, on December 8, 2018.<ref name="McFadden2" />
